open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed-index IPSI bands use a finite-variance Gaussian process, while stable causal limits invalidate the ordinary bootstrap and the critical branch requires inversion of an estimated asymmetric Lévy exponent. The prior QTE run likewise excluded its critical fold-labelled process. Here the normalizer is a generalized inverse of a lower-tail truncated moment, so tail-index and slowly-varying-factor errors are magnified logarithmically; estimating the two-component boundary mark perturbs the jump measure. Pointwise consistency of these inputs does not provide the uniform anti-concentration and certified inversion-error control needed for coverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A feasible plug-in critical-value construction and theorem that the supremum coverage error over the stated second-order tail class and compact h-sets separated within each regime tends to zero, explicitly including nuisance replacement, tail/mark and normalizer estimation, and certified one-dimensional Lévy inversion error.

writing_exemplar.why: Its positivity-challenged nuMoM2b application makes the missing uncertainty quantification for harder odds shifts immediately consequential.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Poor overlap obscures the vegetable-preeclampsia ATE -> moderate IPSI shifts remain interpretable -> bounded multipliers do not answer forceful shifts -> build regime-valid hardening confidence procedures

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt tail-regime estimation and irregular inverse-weight resampling, replacing scalar resample calibration by an empirically fitted marked-law quantile map.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over regular-variation tail calibration, bias centering, and regime-dependent inference for small-denominator weighted sums.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature treats fixed-index IPSI Gaussian theory and fixed-target heavy-tail IPW transitions separately. In hardening IPSI the score itself changes with delta_n: a rare treated observation carries both its outcome residual and a policy-path contrast created because the intervention depends on the observational propensity. The prior QTE construction pushes a one-purpose endpoint score through its own map and expressly withholds the arbitrary critical learned-mark law; joint regular variation and compensation must be rebuilt for this two-component mark. Replacing the mark by the residual is unjustified at finite positive h and becomes valid only at the stable endpoint or under explicit contrast degeneracy.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A triangular marked-point-process convergence theorem giving normalized Gaussian laws for h_n tending to zero, an explicit two-component Lévy-Khintchine triplet for h_n tending to finite positive h, and a residual-only stable law for h_n tending to infinity, with necessary-and-sufficient conditions for disappearance of the contrast mark.

writing_exemplar.why: Its arc from positivity failure to support-respecting odds-shift estimands is the natural target-side narrative before hardening is introduced.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ordinary DML and fixed-index IPSI bounds are calibrated to root-n finite-variance scores and L2 nuisance losses. Under regular variation the operative norm concentrates near e approximately 1/a_n, the stochastic normalization changes with h_n, and propensity estimation perturbs both the denominator and the intervention path. The prior QTE run verified only a target-specific growing-series route and requested a generic learner-transfer theorem, while the transport run could not prove held-out localization of learned extreme weights. A sufficient series example alone would not identify the learner frontier; a converse must show failure when the tail-band condition breaks.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A cross-fitted oracle-equivalence theorem with explicit weighted bias, variance, and product-rate inequalities on a concrete C2 class, generic necessary-and-sufficient tail-band conditions for propensity learners, and a counterexample when they fail, proving fitted-minus-oracle error is negligible under the regime-specific normalization.

method_exemplars.why_closest: The estimator is cross-fitted and orthogonal, but root-n L2 control must be replaced by a hardening-scale norm.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Substituting delta_n into the fixed-functional variance formula does not establish triangular LAN: both the derivative and the rare-score variance move with n. General support-irregularity papers diagnose infinite information for fixed inverse-weight targets but do not identify the drifting IPSI tangent experiment. The earlier QTE work developed upper laws without a local minimax converse, and the ATE retries matched lower bounds only under reservoir-rich shells. Here a fixed shell-localized Le Cam pair fails because delta_n changes both the functional and likelihood scale, while the finite-h experiment retains a compensated two-component Poisson mark.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A convergence-of-experiments and convolution theorem giving the normalized pointwise semiparametric efficiency bound and an attaining estimator when h_n tends to zero, plus matching local asymptotic minimax risk or confidence-length lower bounds and attaining procedures for finite-positive and infinite h_n.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The limit family changes discontinuously with h_n, yet h_n is available only through a tail-defined estimated normalizer; pretesting the regime therefore has nonvanishing error on local transition sequences. Existing adaptive causal procedures hold the target fixed and adapt to tail severity or trimming, not to a jointly drifting score and mark law. Prior threshold and transport proposals show a second obstacle: unknown tail and mark smoothness may require ordered-modulus logarithmic payment or self-similarity. Here the boundary coordinate is itself an estimated propensity, so adaptation must absorb generated-coordinate and second-order tail error as well as regime uncertainty.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An adaptive confidence-set theorem uniformly covering local sequences at both transition boundaries and a union of second-order tail and mark classes, with oracle-order length on separated regimes, or a matching ordered-modulus lower bound identifying the minimal logarithmic penalty and the self-similarity condition that removes it.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates inference that does not require knowing whether causal identification is regular, the closest narrative template for an unknown hardening regime.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Extreme propensities make the limit law unknown -> ordinary bootstrap can fail -> adaptive calibration protects a fixed target -> drifting IPSI requires adaptation across two transitions and unknown tail smoothness

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt tail-sensitive m-selection and bootstrap aggregation that remain valid without knowing the causal score's rate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest adaptive inference result spanning Gaussian and alpha-stable causal-score regimes, though it lacks the intermediate marked family.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute between-class ordered moduli to derive adaptive expected-length lower bounds and construct matching intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution asks whether honest interval length can adapt over nested tail and mark-smoothness classes.

method_exemplars.technique: Use multiscale persistence under self-similarity to make otherwise impossible honest adaptation feasible.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Second-order tail and boundary-mark signals can disappear on isolated scales, the obstruction self-similarity rules out.

literature_map:
Kennedy (2019, JASA, arXiv:1704.00211) defines incremental propensity interventions, derives their efficient influence function, and proves flexible-nuisance Gaussian inference over a fixed multiplier set.
Bonvini, McClean, Branson, and Kennedy (2021, arXiv:2110.10532) review incremental effects as positivity-robust alternatives but do not develop diverging-multiplier asymptotics.
Naimi et al. (2021, Epidemiology, DOI 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001315) apply IPSI to nuMoM2b vegetable intake and preeclampsia for odds multipliers 0.20-5.0 amid visible positivity problems.
Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi (2021, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:1907.04004) extend IPSI efficiency and uniform inference to dropout and longitudinal treatment, still under Gaussian regularity.
McClean et al. (2022/2023, arXiv:2212.03578) develop conditional incremental-effect learners without hardening weak-overlap laws.
Khan and Tamer (2010, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA7372) show thin support can create irregular inverse-weight identification and nonstandard rates.
Crump et al. (2009, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asn055) optimize overlap trimming by changing the target population.
Rothe (2017, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA13141) develops limited-overlap ATE intervals around small effective local sample sizes.
Ma and Wang (2020, JASA, arXiv:1810.11397) obtain Gaussian, compensated infinitely-divisible, and heavy-tail transitions as trimming changes relative to a tail normalizer.
Heiler and Kazak (2021, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.03.025) derive alpha-stable causal-score limits and ordinary-bootstrap failure.
Ma, Sant'Anna, Sasaki, and Ura (2023, arXiv:2304.08974) restore double robustness after extreme-propensity trimming through explicit bias correction.
Hill and Chaudhuri (2025, Econometric Reviews, arXiv:2412.08458) adaptively trim heavy-tailed ATE scores and estimate asymmetric-tail bias.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1608.00060) supply the cross-fitting and orthogonal-score template whose L2 Gaussian conditions do not cover triangular heavy-tail scores.
The central tension is that each fixed IPSI multiplier avoids positivity, yet a diverging multiplier drives its influence score toward the same boundary that causes irregular IPW laws.
No located paper combines diverging binary IPSI, second-order regular variation, a contrast-retaining critical marked law, nonparametric oracle replacement, and uniformly valid plug-in quantiles across all three regimes.
